statement: When you create a market, it inherits your store's default settings. You can override any of these defaults by adding customizations to the market.

identifier: Market customizations and their effects: Catalogs
statement: Which products are available in the market, and at what price.

identifier: Market customizations and their effects: Local currencies
statement: The currency displayed to customers when browsing and paying.

identifier: Market customizations and their effects: Online store
statement: Theme sections, blocks, and content displayed to customers in the market.

identifier: Market customizations and their effects: Domains and languages
statement: The URL structure and language customers experience.

identifier: Market customizations and their effects: Duties and taxes
statement: How taxes are displayed and whether duties are collected at checkout.

identifier: Market customizations and their effects: Business entities
statement: Which legal entity processes payments for the market. Shopify Plus only.
If a market doesn't have a specific customization, then it inherits the value from its parent market. If there's no parent market, then the store default is used.
Different customizations follow different inheritance rules. Some are overridden by the submarket's value, whereas others (like catalogs) are combined.
Customizations are added per market.

Conditions: Conditions define who your market applies to. Conditions can be countries and regions for cross-border selling, company locations for B2B, retail locations for selling in person, or sales channels for selling across channels.
Create markets that target specific states or provinces within a country, so that you can set up different shipping options for different sub-regions. This feature is available as early access.
If your business has different entities globally, then you can configure markets to use business entities in different global regions. Configuring business entities requires the Plus plan.

A market is a set of customers that you define in your store. Markets can be made up of countries or regions for cross-border sales, company locations for B2B sales, retail locations for in-person sales, or sales channels for selling across channels.
When a customer visits your store, it's determined which market they belong to, and the experience that you've configured for that market is displayed.

When a customer visits your online store, their location is determined and they're matched to the appropriate country or region market. The customer then receives the experience that you've configured for that market, including currency, language, product availability, and theme customizations.
A country or region market can contain a single country or multiple countries.
Customers from countries that aren't included in any active market can browse your store, but can't complete a purchase.
Single-country markets contain one country or region. When you create a single-country market, the currency is automatically set to that country's local currency.
Multi-country markets contain more than one country or region. When you create a multi-country market, the currency customization is set to use local currencies by default.
A sub-region market targets a specific state or province, instead of a whole country.
On a sub-region market, you can customize only the shipping options. Everything else, such as currency, catalogs, theme, and domain, is inherited from the parent market.
Country or region markets are available on all Shopify plans. There's no limit to the number of country or region markets you can create.

Retail customers are also part of a regional market based on the POS location's address, which means that a retail transaction can be associated with both a retail market and a country or region market.
B2B markets are more specific than retail markets. Retail markets are more specific than country or region markets.
When a customer qualifies for markets of multiple types, the more specific market type takes priority for how your market customizations take effect.
When you create a Shopify store, the following markets are created for you automatically:

identifier: Review your default markets: Domestic market
statement: Domestic market: Your store's home country or region, as determined by your store's address and currency. This is your domestic market and represents the default customer experience. The country in your domestic market is set as your backup region by default.

identifier: Review your default markets: International market
statement: International market: A curated list of countries or regions where merchants similar to you also sell. This market is inactive by default.
In the **Includes** section, click **Add condition**. This condition defines which of your customers the market is displayed to:
To create a Regional market, select **Regions**, and then select the country or regions to create a market for.

If you create a market as a draft, or if you don't already ship to all the countries in a new market, then the market is inactive by default. Customers in inactive markets can't complete a purchase, and receive the backup region experience when they visit your store.
Before activating a market, ensure that shipping rates are configured for all countries in the market.
You need to have shipping rates configured for all countries and regions that you want to sell to. Markets can be activated only for countries and regions that have shipping rates.
Staff permissions can't be assigned per market. If a staff member has permission to view orders, then they can view orders from all markets.
Only one theme can be published at a time. You can customize your theme per market, but customizations must be applied to your published theme.

Per-market theme customization, such as showing different section content, banners, or layouts for different markets, requires the Advanced plan or higher. On other plans, all markets share the same theme customization.

[Fixed amount discounts](/manual/discounts/discount-types/percentage-fixed-amount) can be created only in your store's default currency. The discount amount is converted to your customer's currency at checkout based on current exchange rates.
Only customers from countries or regions in an active market can check out. If you want to sell to customers in a country or region, then it must be included in an active market.
Creating Regional markets to help you to sell internationally is free for all Shopify plans. However, some customization features are available only to certain plans.
A business entity is the legal entity that processes payments for orders in a market.
By default, all orders in your store are processed through your primary Shopify Payments account, which is associated with your store's home country.
Changing the business entity for a market affects only new orders.

Some regions have regulations about which entity can process payments for customers in that region. Verify with a legal or finance expert that your business entity assignments comply with local requirements.
If a submarket has multiple parent markets with different business entities, then they're prioritized in order of creation. The oldest business entity is used.

identifier: Add a business entity customization to a market
statement: Before you can assign business entities to markets, you need to set up additional Shopify Payments accounts for each legal entity.

Your market settings include a payments card that displays eligible [local payment methods](/manual/international/payments#local-payment-methods), as well as a link to your payment settings where you can activate and customize a variety of payment methods.

identifier: Shopify Payments and other payment providers
statement: The following payment options are compatible with multi-currency processing:

identifier: Shopify Payments and other payment providers
statement: * Shopify Payments credit card payments * Shop Pay * Apple Pay and Google Pay * Paypal Express

identifier: Shopify Payments and other payment providers
statement: If you use a different payment provider, then the local currency feature will only affect how prices are displayed to customers in your store.
When a market contains a country that is eligible for one or more local payment methods, then a payments card is displayed in your market settings with the available local payment methods.
From the payments card, you can activate or deactivate an eligible local payment method.

identifier: Set a currency for a market in Markets
statement: By default, the market's currency is set to the currency for the region that you've selected for your market. For markets that contain more than one region, **Use local currencies** is set as the default instead.

identifier: Set a currency for a market in Markets
statement: You can customize a market's currency at any time.
You can set a specific currency for each market so that your customers can browse, pay, and receive refunds in a currency that's familiar to them.

If a submarket has multiple parent markets with different currency customizations, then the currency that best matches the customer's local currency is used. If no currency matches, then the most recently updated customization is prioritized.
When you use automatic exchange rates, a currency conversion fee is included in the price displayed to your customer. The fee is either 1.5% or 2%, depending on your store's location.
When you use manual exchange rates, the currency conversion fee isn't added to the customer-facing price. Instead, the fee is deducted from your payout.

identifier: ISO country codes for currencies accepted on Shopify Payments through multi currency
statement: Review the list of currencies that you can accept and refund through Shopify Payments, with certain restrictions on specific currencies in France. Local currencies marked with an asterisk (*) aren't available to merchants in France.
When a customer first visits your store, their geographic location is determined by using their IP address, and they're matched to the appropriate market.
If a customer arrives on a market-specific domain, subdomain, or subfolder (for example, yourstore.com/fr/), then they get the experience for that market.
By default, automatic redirection is activated in new stores, and automatic language detection is deactivated.

identifier: Activate a credit card payment provider
statement: You can have only one credit card payment provider activated at a time.

identifier: Activate a credit card payment provider
statement: Only the store owner can add a payment provider.

identifier: Activate a credit card payment provider
statement: If Shopify Payments isn't available in your country, then in the Payment providers section, click Choose a provider
Depending on the requirements of the payment provider, you might be required to submit and verify your bank account information with them so that your store can complete transactions.

identifier: Check payment gateway availability by country
statement: You can [filter available payment providers](https://www.shopify.com/payment-gateways) by country or region to find detailed and updated information about which payment gateways are available in your store's location.

identifier: Are new payment gateways frequently added to Shopify?
statement: Yes, Shopify consistently updates its list of available payment gateways to include new options and geographic expansions.

identifier: What should I do if a provider is listed on the payment gateways page but isn't accessible in my admin?
statement: The payment gateways page lists providers by region, but the options available in your store's admin also depend on your current payment configuration.
To check the transaction fee rates for your location, refer to the Shopify pricing page or contact Shopify Support

identifier: Who is eligible to use Shopify Managed Markets?
statement: To use Shopify Managed Markets, your business needs to be based in the United States, Canada, or the United Kingdom and you need to have Shopify Payments activated on your store.

identifier: Who is eligible to use Shopify Managed Markets?
statement: Managed Markets will be expanding to other regions. Check the Shopify Changelog or your admin for updates.

identifier: Where can I sell with Shopify Managed Markets?
statement: Shopify Managed Markets supports selling to 150+ regions. Some high-risk currency markets (including Argentina, Turkey, Lebanon, and Venezuela) are not currently supported due to currency volatility and compliance requirements.

identifier: What happens to my existing international markets if I activate Shopify Managed Markets?
statement: You select which markets you'd like to activate with Shopify Managed Markets. Shopify then migrates any existing international market settings and enables all features in eligible markets.

identifier: Multi-currency payouts now available in Australia and France
statement: We've expanded Multi-Currency Payouts for eligible Shopify Payments merchants to Australia and France.

identifier: Multi-currency payouts now available in Australia and France
statement: Merchants in Australia can now receive payouts in 13 currencies: AUD, NZD, USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, NOK, SEK, DKK, CHF, JPY, SGD and HKD. All 13 can be paid into an Australian bank account, or you can add an account in the US, New Zealand, the UK, Canada or the eurozone for those currencies.

identifier: Multi-currency payouts now available in Australia and France
statement: Merchants in France can now receive payouts in 18 currencies: EUR, AUD, CAD, CHF, CZK, DKK, GBP, HKD, HUF, JPY, NOK, NZD, PLN, RON, SEK, SGD, USD and ZAR. EUR remains your default payout currency, and other currencies are paid into additional bank accounts you add.
